advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the new local-repo SHA resolution requirement in rebar.attach_commits is an intended, documented breaking narrowing (or relax it to warn/skip for unfetched-but-valid SHAs) to preserve the prior accept-any-string contract.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:720 `unresolvable = commit_impact.unresolvable_shas([r["sha"] for r in records], tracker)` followed by `raise RebarError(... did not resolve to a commit in this repository; nothing was recorded)`
`rebar.attach_commits` is a public surface: src/rebar/__init__.py:105 imports it and :165 lists it in the export set

Consumer evidence of narrowing: tests/interfaces/store/test_commits_on_ticket.py previously passed placeholder SHAs and now must synthesize real ones — the diff replaces `rebar.attach_commits(tid, ["abc123", {"sha": "def456", ...}])` with `a, b = _real_shas(...)`, and the new `_real_shas` docstring states 'attach_commits validates that every SHA resolves to a commit in the repository (all-or-nothing), so these store-semantics tests need genuine SHAs rather than placeholder strings'

Tension with the feature's own design: close_precheck._check_file_impact_vs_diff treats an unreadable attached SHA as skippable because it 'may legitimately live in another clone (or simply be unfetched)', yet the attach seam now rejects exactly such a SHA at record time
advisory.finding: The public exported library function `rebar.attach_commits(ticket_id, commits)` narrows its accepted input: it now validates that every SHA resolves to a commit in the local repo and rejects the entire batch with a RebarError otherwise, whereas previously any non-empty SHA string (or {sha,...} dict) was recorded unconditionally. Existing callers that attached SHAs not present in the local clone — a case the diff's own close-check acknowledges ('an attached SHA may legitimately live in another clone') — now fail at attach time.
scenarios: An author on a fresh clone that has not fetched the target commit calls rebar.attach_commits with a valid-but-unfetched SHA and is now rejected where it previously succeeded
A programmatic library consumer that recorded commit SHAs from an external source (not present locally) now raises RebarError

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate attach_commits SHAs against the caller-supplied repo_root (fall back to tracker parent only when repo_root is None) instead of always using os.path.dirname(tracker).
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:720 `unresolvable = commit_impact.unresolvable_shas([r["sha"] for r in records], tracker)`
commit_impact.py:135-147 `code_root_for` returns `os.path.dirname(str(tracker))` and `unresolvable_shas` passes that to `invalid_commit_shas`, so `repo_root` is never consulted for validation.
dropped.finding: attach_commits SHA validation ignores the caller-supplied repo_root: unresolvable_shas uses code_root_for(tracker)=os.path.dirname(str(tracker)) to pick the git repo, while tracker_dir/append_event honor repo_root. When REBAR_TRACKER_DIR points outside the code repo (tracker parent != repo_root), SHAs are validated against the wrong git repository.
scenarios: A store where REBAR_TRACKER_DIR is set to a directory whose parent is not the code repo, with an explicit repo_root passed to attach_commits.
